client_brief:
Sable and Finch Realty: Sable and Finch listing tour

Project overview
Sable and Finch Realty sells character homes along the North Shore to move up families who are choosing carefully between a small number of houses. We are hiring an expert to turn the supplied working files into Sable and Finch listing tour, landscape master and vertical cut, Sable and Finch evening exterior set and listing cover, and Open house card run, twelve listings.

What we will provide
source_video_files/ (7 measured short files); source_audio_files/ (1 measured WAV file); motion_source_metadata.json; source_video_files/ (7 measured short files); source_audio_files/ (1 measured WAV file); sablefinch_exteriors/ (11 stills, camera scale); sablefinch_open_house_card.pdf; sablefinch_listings.csv; sablefinch_look_reference.jpg; sablefinch_facts_and_disclosure.txt; sablefinch_mark_scan.png. Every file must be accounted for in the final manifest; it may be used, retained as reference, superseded, or rejected with a reason.

Scope and deliverables
- Sable and Finch listing tour, landscape master and vertical cut: A deliberate 24-second-or-shorter edit assembled from the 7 supplied short clips using an explicit timeline, plus one platform reframe and three checked poster frames. 
- Sable and Finch evening exterior set and listing cover: The dusk exteriors brought to one warm evening target (one white point, one black point, one treatment of the lit porch against the sky), plus one licensed camera scale streetscape frame graded into the same world, and from that set the cover still and the...
- Open house card run, twelve listings: One press PDF at one page per listing for all twelve active listings, derived from the team's own printed card, with every mapped field verified present in the template before the merge and every page proofed after it. 

Non-negotiables
- Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
- Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
- Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.

Source-media note
The supplied package contains 7 video files totaling 35.294 seconds, 0 with embedded audio, and 1 separate audio file. These measured values are the production limits.

Working process
Please begin with an inventory and risk pass, submit the first proof or direction at the stated checkpoint, then revise against consolidated feedback. We are hiring for judgment: flag contradictions early, make the strongest defensible choice, and document any source limitation rather than hiding it.

Contract
$5,000-$12,000 fixed; target delivery 4 to 6 weeks; direction approval, first-production proof, and two consolidated revision rounds. Final handoff includes the delivery manifest, editable sources where scoped, final exports, and a concise production note.

source_provenance.statement: The scenario is synthesized from the repository's laundered Upwork and Freelancer source anchors. It is not represented as a verbatim live listing.
source_provenance.original_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork post 'Real Estate Listing / Property Tour Video Editor' quoted in the ledger's grounding_note, in which a realtor supplies raw handheld property walkthrough clips plus a few exterior shots and asks for a polished branded listing tour: trim and sequence the best shots into a sizzle, add branded lower thirds carrying the address, the price and the agent, an intro title and an end card, one consistent colour grade, exported for MLS and the listing website plus a vertical social cut and a thumbnail. The real post names no company, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional brand Sable and Finch Realty and the agents stay unnamed. REASONABLY ENRICHED into the fuller commission that client actually needed rather than the video edit alone: the same team prints an open house card for every active listing, so the engagement carries the card run as a genuine record per page variable data job off their own existing printed card, and the captions are delivered as something the team can retype next week rather than baked pixels, because the post's own reason for hiring (four or five listings a month, prices move) makes editability the whole point. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) is what makes that honest: a real press PDF converts into a live merge template headlessly, and HTML authoring produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes.

price_band_and_audience: A 1.2 million dollar coastal single family listing sold to move up buyers aged roughly 35 to 48 with children, choosing between three or four comparable houses in the same school district. The band is load bearing. At this price the tour has to be slow, warm and near neutral, with long held frames, restrained captioning and an evening cover: the buyer is reassuring herself about a large decision, and calm reads as confidence. Push the same material into a saturated, fast cut, caption heavy treatment with hard cuts on every beat and it reads as a 400,000 dollar starter home listing and the move up buyer stops watching, which is the exact failure the team is paying to avoid. Push the other way into a near silent, near black, no text luxury film and it misprices the house upward and confuses buyers who genuinely need the bed count and the school district on screen. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Residential real estate: a boutique agent team listing coastal single family homes on Massachusetts' North Shore.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2016, Marblehead, Massachusetts, a four agent residential team running four or five listings a month.
brand_identity.about: Sable and Finch Realty sells character homes along the North Shore to move up families who are choosing carefully between a small number of houses. We present a property the way a buyer wants to feel about it: calm, warm and reassuring. Our work is quiet on purpose, because at this price calm reads as confidence.
brand_identity.audience: Move up buyers roughly 35 to 48 with children, weighing this house against three or four comparable homes in the same school district, who need the facts on screen and the feeling in the frame.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Homes around and above 1.2 million dollars, the established coastal middle of the market. Presentation sits between a fast starter home listing and a near silent luxury film, and must read as neither.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet, warm text serif for names and headings paired with a restrained sans for facts and captions. Type stays small and calm: address, price, beds and baths and school district carried plainly, never loud, never dense. Evening warmth over crisp cool.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, measured, reassuring, never a hard sell. Example: "Two streets back from the water, shingled, and the porch light is already on."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no packaged brand kit. Last season's open house card survives only as the printer's press PDF, and the on screen captions have always been rebuilt by hand each listing. Colour and type live in prior collateral rather than in a guideline anyone can hand over.
brand_identity.values: Honest presentation of a real property. Every figure a buyer relies on, the price, the bed and bath count, the school district and the disclosure line, must be exactly right on every piece.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_exteriors/ (11 stills, camera scale)
assets_supplied.kind: Dusk exterior stills of the house shot by the team's photographer across about twenty minutes of falling light.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The dusk exteriors. Our favourite is the one with the porch lights on."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The two frames the team likes best were exposed for the lit porch interior, so the sky across the upper third is clipped flat and a highlight recovery move on those frames returns a result in which nothing visibly changes. Separately one of the two is about two and a half degrees off level, and levelling it eats exactly the roofline that the cover crop needs to keep, so straightening and cropping cannot both be satisfied on that frame.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_open_house_card.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The team's existing printed open house card from last season, supplied as the template for the run.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's card. We want the same card for every listing."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Printed, the card shows four clearly separated blocks. Its text was actually set as one continuous flow, so the conversion exposes far coarser frame granularity than the printed page suggests. Worse, the mapping readout omits one run from the middle of that story while keeping its line break, so the readout still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid on those offsets and the placeholder step reports success, and the fields past the omission simply never land.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_listings.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twelve active listings: address, town, price, beds, baths, square feet, school district, open house window, agent line.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "All twelve of our current listings. The open house times are already correct."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the twelve addresses are long enough that at trim they run past the card's fixed measure. A fixed text frame does not spill and does not flag: it simply stops rendering, so those records come out truncated in the middle of a street name while the merge reports success and the page count is exactly right. One further row carries a price with a range rather than a single figure, which reads as an error on a printed card.

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_look_reference.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A warm still the team pulled from a tour video by another firm that they admire, supplied purely as a look reference.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Roughly the feeling we want. Warm, slow, not shiny."

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_facts_and_disclosure.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the listing facts for the featured house, the caption copy, and the brokerage disclosure line that must appear on every printed card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The facts and the disclosure. The disclosure wording cannot be changed."

assets_supplied.name: sablefinch_mark_scan.png
assets_supplied.kind: The Sable and Finch lockup, a small finch perched on a branch emblem beside the SABLE AND FINCH wordmark, the only surviving copy, exported small from the team's old email signature.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our little finch logo. We only have this one small copy of it, off an old email footer."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a low resolution raster with soft anti aliased edges and a faint halo, and the mark is Finch Gold sitting on a Shell ground at low contrast. A default trace reads the halo as edge and returns a furry multi node outline, and at that low contrast a luminance or ink level selection closes the finch's eye counter and merges the fine branch strokes. Nothing shows at screen size: the trace looks clean until it is placed at the card's roughly fourteen millimetre lockup and the end card size, where the eye fills in and the branch gaps close. The mark has to be selected by its own gold hue and thresholded to a clean bi level before the trace, and confirmed at reproduction size rather than on screen.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Which visible beats in the measured short clips actually cut together without a continuity jump, duplicate action, or missing subject.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Filenames and source duration do not establish visual continuity. The first assembled proof is the earliest reliable evidence.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Replace or reorder source ranges, shorten the piece, and rebuild the EDL around the strongest continuous action.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A technically valid render feels accidental or implies an action that the source never completes.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the approved horizontal composition survives the required vertical or square reframe with the subject and essential interface or product detail still visible.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The crop depends on the actual chosen ranges and subject position inside each rendered frame.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Choose a different source range for the platform version or use fit instead of fill and revise the surrounding design treatment.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The platform export is correctly sized but loses the person, product, or interface that gives the shot meaning.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the separately supplied audio remains intelligible and appropriately synchronized after the final duration and crop decisions.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: This can be judged only on the final rendered sequence, not from a successful operation response.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebalance or shorten the selected audio passage and render again against the locked picture.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The picture is polished but the spoken information is clipped, mistimed, or inconsistent.

acceptance_snapshot: The open house run is one page per listing for all twelve, and every page is correct: every field present, nothing truncated at the measure, and the disclosure line on all of them.

The capture generation split is established by reading each clip's true dimensions rather than by its filename, and the master and vertical ceilings follow from that reading: the phone generation rooms and the portrait pass are named as ceilings, not discovered by a viewer later.
The tour reads as one calm evening piece: one warm target across every graded frame, one pace, and no moment where the picture visibly changes generation mid sequence.

No delivered video or still exceeds the pixel dimensions of the material it was made from, and no crop's returned tradeoff record carries an upscale entry. A cover that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The vertical cut is genuinely derived from the master rather than being a separately reasoned edit, and its size ceiling is stated honestly rather than asserted.
Every supplied asset is listed in the delivery manifest as used, reference-only, superseded, or rejected with a concrete reason; no input disappears silently.
Final files open successfully, use unambiguous names, match the stated dimensions and formats, and include editable sources only where the scoped deliverable requires them.
The edit never claims more source duration or source audio than motion_source_metadata.json records, and every delivered time range is traceable to the final EDL.

why_not_vlm: A generated video would replace the supplied people, products, interfaces, locations, and finite recorded actions rather than edit them. This task is scored on traceability to measured source ranges, final framing, and truthful use of separate audio, which a newly generated clip cannot satisfy.
